E9_lora_linear_fused_classification.classification: NEITHER pure rounding-placement (the elementwise delta is too large and too structured for that, unlike GeGLU's/LayerNorm's disclosed round-once-vs-cascade divergence) NOR a demonstrated formula/indexing bug at the single-call level (the existing F32/CPU oracle suite passes, and the module doc's GEMM-operand-form derivation checks out algebraically against candle's own Op::Matmul backward rule for both dA^T and dB). The evidence is consistent with an esc-044-CLASS compounding divergence: a small, individually bf16-bound-consistent per-call difference (not caught by the F32/CPU-only oracle, which has no BF16/CUDA leg to catch a BF16-specific rounding difference at all) that accumulates additively through candle's own backward walk across 28 layers, reaching a large, layer-0-dominant magnitude. The exact bit-level origin (which of the internal GEMMs' CUDA-issued form differs from what cuBLAS issues for the eager graph) was NOT isolated within this round's budget -- the concrete next artifact is a BF16/CUDA production-width oracle for LowRankResidualLinear's own bwd against candle's own eager-composition autograd, mirroring geglu_oracles.rs's/layer_norm_oracles.rs's existing BF16 disclosure tests, which do not exist for this op today.

E10_flash_reconciliation.reconciliation: Round 6's E3 found flash near-orthogonal (or worse -- negative cosine) to jammi's own f32 truth on the ACTIVATION-gradient axis (boundary.1-7, cosine -0.34 to +0.11, gradient norm 2.4x-7.7x too large) at exactly the layers that carry 83.7% of the total WEIGHT-gradient mass (E8's own layer-mass table) -- so this is NOT a 'negligible mass, don't care' region; it is the highest-leverage part of the network. Yet flash's own per-tensor WEIGHT-gradient cosine at those SAME layers' LoRA A/B tensors is good (0.74-0.85, comparable to every other tested arm), which is why E4's full-224-tensor weight-gradient cosine (0.790) never surfaced this defect. The reconciliation: boundary.i = dL/d(output of encoder layer i) is the CUMULATIVE residual-stream gradient -- the sum of every downstream (layer i+1..27) path's contribution flowing back through that one point, so it inherits and compounds whatever numerical divergence flash's own backward introduces at every subsequent layer's attention block. The LoRA weight gradient at layer i, by contrast, is a LOCAL quantity (dA_i/dB_i depend only on that layer's own sublayer's dy and its own local activation, via the two short GEMM chains E9 quotes) that does not itself have to reconstruct the cumulative residual-stream magnitude correctly to stay direction-aligned. E4 does not 'average away' a negligible defect; it measures a genuinely DIFFERENT gradient quantity that is structurally insulated from the specific compounding mechanism the boundary axis exposes.

one_paragraph_mechanism_reading: Round 6's headline (production block-fused, 0.610, is the WORST bf16 weight-gradient arm vs jammi's own f32 truth, worse than all-eager's 0.810) does not reproduce at seed43/b4-s128 (0.258 > 0.104) or at b8-s128/seed42 (0.843 > 0.773) -- it is a property of the ONE originally-measured cell, not of the production kernel stack. The full-224-tensor concatenated cosine this whole investigation has used as its headline metric is dominated, at every config, by 4-5 early-layer tensors (layers 0-4 carry 83.7% of the f32-truth gradient's L2^2 mass) whose own cosine is the worst in the network because the BACKWARD pass accumulates the most compounded rounding by the time it reaches layer 0 -- the same 'compounding is invisible at one call, key the oracle on GROWTH' mechanism esc-044 named, generalized from one op's forward to the whole stack's backward. attention_block_fused and the cast_scale/cast_add pair are provably value-neutral (bit-identical baseline cosine across all three configs); geglu_fused and layer_norm_fused are large but SIGN-FLIPPING movers, consistent with their own module docs' disclosed, tested, individually-defensible round-once-vs-cascade bf16 rounding choice rather than a directional defect; lora_linear_fused is the one op whose disable is robustly positive at all three configs despite passing its existing (F32/CPU-only) oracle suite cleanly, and its own fused-vs-near-eager delta at layer 0's dominant-mass Wqkv tensor is large and structured (not few-ulp) with an r(L) that grows from 0.32 at the last layer to 0.60-0.75 at the first nine -- an esc-044-class compounding signature this round could not fully bisect to a single line within budget, for which the missing artifact is a BF16/CUDA production-width oracle this op does not have today. Flash's severe early-layer ACTIVATION-gradient defect (E3, cosine down to -0.34) sits at the same high-mass layers without corrupting the WEIGHT-gradient cosine there (0.74-0.85), because the two gradient quantities are structurally different: one is the cumulative residual-stream signal every downstream layer's error compounds into, the other a local per-layer computation insulated from that specific accumulation.

lead_probe_softmax_isolation_ledger_row_.rounding_placement_finding: candle_nn::ops::softmax (jammi's PRODUCTION eager fallback, candle-nn-0.11.0/src/ops.rs:22-29) does NOT upcast to F32 anywhere: max_keepdim/broadcast_sub/exp/sum_keepdim/broadcast_div all execute directly at the input dtype (BF16 here) -- a 5-op BF16 cascade, no f32 accumulator at all. jammi's OWN fused softmax (SoftmaxLastDimFused) already accumulates row-max/exp/row-sum in F32 and rounds to BF16 exactly once (softmax.rs:1151-1153) -- i.e. the FUSED arm is the one closer to torch's own reference discipline (modeling_modernbert.py: F32 softmax, BF16 cast of probs before the PV GEMM), not the eager one. Separately: `raw_scores` itself (BEFORE softmax runs, either arm) is BF16 unless JAMMI_ROUND5_UPCAST_SCORES=1 -- OFF by default in every run here and in every production call site -- upcasts q/k to F32 for the scores GEMM specifically. Round 6's own E6 already measured that exact upcast-to-match-torch diagnostic under this round's Gaussian LoRA init and found it did NOT help (block-eager arm's boundary.1-18 cosine vs jammi f32 truth got WORSE, 0.6618->0.5845, upcast on vs off) -- so 'make eager softmax's scores F32 like torch' is not evidenced as the right fix target either, independent of this round's own softmax-isolation instability finding.

lead_probe_2_H1_H2_ledger_row_258.overall_answer_to_lead: H1 (shared bf16 magnitude-blowup mechanism) is not supported by the ||g|| ratio data: none of the three ops' ablations pulls the ratio toward 1 at the layers its own cosine improves, and baseline's own ratio was never dramatically blown up on this axis to begin with (nothing like 5-13x) -- the cited 5-13x finding likely reflects a different comparison (jammi vs torch) than jammi-vs-its-own-f32-truth. H2 (additivity/coupling) is answered by data already in this artifact: neither hypothesis's predicted pattern (pairs~=0.81, or singles+pairs summing linearly) matches -- pairs are LOWER than either constituent single, and the triple EXCEEDS all_off. The softmax-standalone arm was already measured (part of the first lead probe) and shows the same seed/shape-fragile pattern geglu_fused/layer_norm_fused show, not a cleaner isolated signal. No new binary build was required to answer any of this -- all three answers come from data this round already collected on the block binary (target-r6-base, git_rev 8924b30), cross-validated digit-for-digit against the lead's independently-built --ablate-each-op tool on a100d.
